title: Sonnet 26
author: Edmund Spenser
intro: English poet Edmund Spenser lived from 1552-1599. Read his poem “Sonnet 26” below. Use the information from the poem to answer the questions that follow.
lines: Sweet is the rose, but grows upon a briar;
Sweet is the juniper, but sharp his bough,
Sweet is the eglantine,¹ but pricketh near;
Sweet is the fir bloom, but his branch is rough;
Sweet is the cypress, but his rind is tough;
Sweet is the nut, but bitter is his pill;
Sweet is the broom flower, but yet sour enough;
And sweet is moly,² but his root is ill.
So every sweet with sour is tempered still,
That maketh it be coveted the more:
For easy things, that may be got at will,
Most sorts of men do set but little store.
Why then should I account of little pain,
That endless pleasure shall unto me gain!
